subject.title: Add maxThreads config for local embedding (node-llama-cpp)

question: Should OpenClaw add an official local llama CPU thread tuning config under `memorySearch.local`, and should it map to `getLlama.maxThreads`, context `threads`, or another narrower shape?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but repository policy treats new config/default surfaces as product/API decisions and the dependency exposes both instance-level and context-level thread controls.

options.title: Approve a narrow thread knob
options.body: Add an optional advanced `memorySearch.local` thread-control field, keep defaults unchanged, document the exact node-llama mapping, and add focused tests.

options.title: Defer to a broader local llama tuning design
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers define a cohesive local llama tuning surface for CPU, GPU, context, batching, and NUMA behavior.

options.title: Reject canonical config expansion
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's local embedding config minimal and direct advanced CPU tuning to custom plugins or external embedding providers.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow thread knob
recommendation.body: Add an optional advanced `memorySearch.local` thread-control field, keep defaults unchanged, document the exact node-llama mapping, and add focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent central-file ownership and the decision is about public config surface growth in the local embedding path.
